Jorge Assis, PhD // Nord University, Norway // biodiversityDS, Centre of Marine Sciences, Portugal

Model evaluation

Model evaluation with random cross-validation

biodiversityDS .

Random cross-validation is a method to evaluate the performance of a model by splitting the data into training and testing sets multiple times. This approach can generate test datasets with low level of independence.

# read occurrence records (presences) and transform to spatial object
library(terra)
presences <- read.table("../Data/Text delimited/species_presence_records.csv", sep = ";", header = TRUE)
presences <- vect(presences, geom = c("Lon", "Lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")
S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# download layers for present conditions
variables <- list(var1 = c("thetao", "mean", "depthmean"), var2 = c("o2", "mean", "depthmean"),
    var3 = c("phyc", "mean", "depthmean"))
environmentalLayers <- download_multiple_layers(variables = variables, experiment = c("baseline"),
    decade = c(2010))
names(environmentalLayers) <- c("Temperature", "Oxygen", "Productivity")
# plot layers
plot(environmentalLayers, axes = TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# develop a study region layer
myStudyRegion <- studyRegion(rasterLayers=environmentalLayers, # SpatRaster of layers
                             presences=presences, # presence records
                             distanceThreshold=200000, # distance from records in meters
                             topographyLayer = "../Data/Raster data/Bathymetry.tif", # bathymetry layer
                             verticalPref=c(-15,-300)) # known vertical distribution
# inspect the study region layer
plot(myStudyRegion, main="Study region", col="#979797", axes=TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# crop the environmental layers to the extent of the study region
environmentalLayers <- crop(environmentalLayers, myStudyRegion)
# mask the environmental layers with the study region
environmentalLayers <- mask(environmentalLayers, myStudyRegion)
# plot the masked environmental layers
plot(environmentalLayers, axes = TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# generate pseudo-absences and combine presences and absences into a unique object
absences <- pseudoAbsences(rasterLayers = environmentalLayers, presences = presences, n = 1000)
presences$PA <- 1
absences$PA <- 0
records <- rbind(absences, presences)
# generate a landmass for representation
landmass <- vect("../Data/Vector data/Landmass/landmass.shp")
landmassMed <- crop(landmass, myStudyRegion)
# plot records
plot(landmassMed, main = "Species Records", col = "#D4D4D4", border = "#D4D4D4", axes = TRUE)
plot(records, y = "PA", col = c("#c29431", "#043259"), pch = 16, cex = 0.5, add = TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# extract environmental values and make an object with all information to model
modelData <- generateModelData(records, environmentalLayers, method = "random", bootstrapRounds = 10,
    paMinimum = 100, paRatio = 1)
## Warning ::  190  records were removed because they have NA values in the environmental data
S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
modelData$plotDatasets

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# fit a brt model to the dataset
model <- trainModel(modelData, algorithm = "brt")
# predict the distribution with the model over a raster stack
prediction <- predictModel(model = model, newData = environmentalLayers)
# map the predicted distribution
plot(prediction$rasterLayer, main = "Predicted species distribution", col = rev(topo.colors(100)))

Model evaluation with blocks cross-validation

biodiversityDS .

Blocks cross-validation is a method to evaluate the performance of a model by splitting the data into training and testing sets multiple times. This approach can generate test datasets with high level of independence.

# Inspect spatial autocorrelation in the layers
sacAnalysis <- sac(environmentalLayers = environmentalLayers)
sacAnalysis$distance
## [1] 66.66667
S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# Inspect spatial autocorrelation in the layers
sacAnalysis$plot

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# extract environmental values and make an object with all information to model
modelData <- generateModelData(records, environmentalLayers, method = "blocks", bootstrapRounds = 10,
    paMinimum = 100, paRatio = 1, sacDist = sacAnalysis$distance)
## Warning ::  190  records were removed because they have NA values in the environmental data

# map the predicted distribution
plot(prediction$rasterLayer, main = "Predicted species distribution", col = rev(topo.colors(100)))

Variable relative importance

Inspecting relative importance of variables to assess their potential ecological role in the models.

# get the variable relative contribution
modelVarContrib <- variableContribution(model, rasterLayers = environmentalLayers)

S5 // Developing Species Distribution Models in R

Model Reclassification

Minimum training presence threshold

biodiversityDS .

Minimum training presence threshold is the lowest predicted value associated with at least 90% of observed presence records. This threshold is commonly used to reclassify the predicted distribution into binary presence/absence.

# read occurrence records (presences) and transform to spatial object
library(terra)
presences <- read.table("../Data/Text delimited/species_presence_records.csv", sep = ";", header = TRUE)
presences <- vect(presences, geom = c("Lon", "Lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")
S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# download layers for present conditions
variables <- list(var1 = c("thetao", "mean", "depthmean"), var2 = c("o2", "mean", "depthmean"),
    var3 = c("phyc", "mean", "depthmean"))
environmentalLayers <- download_multiple_layers(variables = variables, experiment = c("baseline"),
    decade = c(2010))
# change for friendly names
names(environmentalLayers) <- c("Temperature", "Oxygen", "Productivity")
# plot layers
plot(environmentalLayers, axes = TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# develop a study region layer
myStudyRegion <- studyRegion(rasterLayers=environmentalLayers, # SpatRaster of layers
                             presences=presences, # presence records
                             distanceThreshold=200000, # distance from records in meters
                             topographyLayer = "../Data/Raster data/Bathymetry.tif", # bathymetry layer
                             verticalPref=c(-15,-300)) # known vertical distribution
# inspect the study region layer
plot(myStudyRegion, main="Study region", col="#979797", axes=TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# crop the environmental layers to the extent of the study region
environmentalLayers <- crop(environmentalLayers, myStudyRegion)
# mask the environmental layers with the study region
environmentalLayers <- mask(environmentalLayers, myStudyRegion)
# plot the masked environmental layers
plot(environmentalLayers, axes = TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# generate pseudo-absences and combine presences and absences into a unique object
absences <- pseudoAbsences(rasterLayers = environmentalLayers, presences = presences, n = 1000)
presences$PA <- 1
absences$PA <- 0
records <- rbind(absences, presences)
# generate a landmass for representation
landmass <- vect("../Data/Vector data/Landmass/landmass.shp")
landmassMed <- crop(landmass, myStudyRegion)
# plot records
plot(landmassMed, main = "Species Records", col = "#D4D4D4", border = "#D4D4D4", axes = TRUE)
plot(records, y = "PA", col = c("#c29431", "#043259"), pch = 16, cex = 0.5, add = TRUE)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# Inspect spatial autocorrelation in the layers
sacAnalysis <- sac(environmentalLayers = environmentalLayers)
sacAnalysis$distance
## [1] 66.66667
S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# extract environmental values and make an object with all information to model
modelData <- generateModelData(records, environmentalLayers, method = "blocks", bootstrapRounds = 10,
    sacDist = sacAnalysis$distance, paMinimum = 100, paRatio = 1)
## Warning ::  190  records were removed because they have NA values in the environmental data
S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# fit a brt model to the dataset
model <- trainModel(modelData, algorithm = "brt")
# predict the distribution with the model over a raster stack
prediction <- predictModel(model = model, newData = environmentalLayers)
# map the predicted distribution
plot(prediction$rasterLayer, main = "Predicted species distribution", col = rev(topo.colors(100)))

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# reclass the predicted distribution into binary presence/absence using the minimum train
# threshold
observed <- records$PA
predicted <- extract(prediction$rasterLayer, records, ID = FALSE)[, 1]

# inspect the predicted values at observed sites
hist(predicted, xlab = "Predicted value", col = "#C8E6FA", breaks = 100)

S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# infer the minimum training presence threshold
performance <- modelPerformance(observed, predicted, index = "minimumTrain90")
performance
##   criteria threshold   auc   auc.prg omission.rate sensitivity specificity
## 1      P10   0.61375 0.946 0.9206792        0.0982      0.9018       0.875
##   prop.correct  Kappa     aicc deviance boyce    tss prevalence.obs
## 1     0.888251 0.7766 1198.684 1194.677 0.984 0.7768      0.4944388
##   prevalence.pred
## 1          0.5091
S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# apply the minimum training presence threshold
threshold <- performance$threshold
threshold
## [1] 0.61375
rclmat <- data.frame(from = c(0, threshold), to = c(threshold, 1), becomes = c(0, 1))
rclmat
##      from      to becomes
## 1 0.00000 0.61375       0
## 2 0.61375 1.00000       1
S6 // Performance of Species Distribution Models

biodiversityDS .
# reclassify prediction into presence/absence
predictionPresentReclass <- classify(prediction$rasterLayer, rclmat)

# plot the predicted distribution reclassified into presence/absence
plot(predictionPresentReclass, main = "Predicted species distribution", col = c("#C8E6FA", "#0c2f4d"))
